claims.text: A hybrid high-throughput CALPHAD and machine-learning framework can accurately predict melting temperature and entropy of fusion for refractory high-entropy alloys.
The hybrid framework can overcome both the unreliability of Lennard-Jones molecular dynamics and the scarcity of extreme-temperature experimental data.
Multi-component refractory HEAs such as Nb-Mo-Ta-W-V have disordered BCC or FCC solid-solution matrices.
Experimental melting data for refractory HEAs is sparse or unreliable because their melting points exceed 2000 °C.
High-throughput CALPHAD can screen thousands of compositions for phase stability and approximate melting behavior.
Machine-learning models using Holder means of elemental properties and structural descriptors can predict melting temperature, entropy of fusion, and heat capacity.
Prediction accuracy depends strongly on the quality and population of the thermodynamic database.
For the Al-Cr-Fe-Mn-Ti system, the relevant CALPHAD method is limited to a database-optimized range including Al below 25 at.%.
High-entropy theory does not apply to systems with very large heats of formation, including oxides.
Lattice disorder becomes dominant near the melting point, with a transition from stacking-fault formation to lattice disorder.
Atomic-size mismatch and lattice distortion drive the entropy of fusion in disordered HEAs.
Molecular dynamics using Lennard-Jones potentials alone is unreliable for multi-component HEAs.
Lennard-Jones molecular dynamics fails because it does not capture the complex multi-body interactions in HEAs.
CALPHAD phase-fraction screening can establish phase stability before property prediction.

Holder-mean machine-learning models can extrapolate melting thermodynamics from elemental and structural trends and capture the high-entropy contribution without explicit liquid-phase atomistic simulation.
The workflow will identify alloys with melting temperatures above 1250 °C and selected BCC or L2_1 phase fractions.
Errors in predicted melting properties will be below 10% and significantly lower than errors from pure molecular dynamics or conventional CALPHAD.
The workflow can enable screening of vast compositional spaces where experimental data is unavailable.
Predictions for less-studied systems and extreme temperatures are uncertain because database parameters depend on available experimental optimization and validation data.
Training on ordered compounds may reduce prediction accuracy for disordered HEAs because lattice-distortion effects are not fully represented.
